A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adhesion of infected red blood cell (IRBC) onto brain endothelium induces the transfer of parasite material to the endothelial cell plasma membrane, followed by an engulfing of the IRBC by the endothelial cell in a trogocyto-like process.

the adhesion of infected red blood cell to endothelial cells is a complex process involving several mechanisms that can be divided into two phases: the first phase involves the transfer of material to endothelial cells and the second phase involves the engulfment of the infected red blood cell.

the adhesion of Plasmodium falcaparum on the brain endothelium induces the opening of the tight junctions, and that this process is associated with the transfer of parasite antigens to the endothelial cell plasma membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRBC/brain EC junction is formed by a cup-like structure, and that this adhesion induces the transfer of material and the opening of the tight junctions.
IRBC/EC interaction induces the opening of EC junctions and that this phenomenon is dependent on the cytoskeleton.
